add_info: The river IJzer originates in Kassel, France, and flows into the North Sea at Nieuwpoort via the Ganzepoot. The IJzer is 78 km long, 45 km of which lie within Belgian territory. The tidal section of the IJzer is approximately 3 km long and extends from the mouth of the river into the North Sea to the Ganzepoot lock complex.
The mesohaline zone of the Zeeschelde (salinity: 5–18) is situated between Zandvliet (Dutch–Belgian border) and Antwerpen (Belgium).
The oligohaline zone (salinity 0.5–5) is situated between Antwerpen and Rupelmonde and includes the Rupel River.
The freshwater zone of the Zeeschelde is situated between Rupelmonde and Gent, including the River Durme (limnetic zone: <0.5).

add_info: This index was developed for freshwater tributaries affected by tidal influences. The index is comprising four metrics. Metric values were calculated using data (fykefishing) obtained within one year (3 seasons).
